AG.name: Antigua and Barbuda

laws.name: Data Protection Act, 2013
laws.citation: No. 10 of 2013; s.2 health is sensitive personal data; s.18(1)(a) explicit consent; no transfer-abroad section

AG.regulator: Information Commissioner (Freedom of Information Act 2004; no website located)
AG.notes: Act gazetted 7 Nov 2013 with no separate commencement clause, so treated as in force from publication. Health is sensitive and needs explicit consent (s.18(1)(a)). The Act has no cross-border transfer section, so explicit consent plus disclosure of US processing is enough. Regulator is the FOI Act Information Commissioner; no website or recent enforcement found. No amendment or replacement bill located (Oct 2026).

BB.name: Barbados

laws.name: Data Protection Act, 2019
laws.citation: Act 2019-29; s.2 sensitive list omits health; s.9(1)(a) written consent for sensitive data; ss.22, 26(a) transfers with consent derogation; s.50 registration

BB.notes: Read from the April 2019 Bill; DLA Piper's summary of the enacted Act gives the same s.2 list, which omits health (genetic and biometric data are sensitive and need written consent, s.9(1)(a)), hence 'personal'; confirm against the enacted text. Transfers: s.22 adequacy, s.26(a) consent derogation. In force 31 Mar 2021 except registration ss.50-52, 55-57 (DataGuidance, Oct 2023); once proclaimed, a non-resident controller must register and nominate a Barbados representative (s.50(3)).

BS.name: Bahamas

laws.name: Data Protection (Privacy of Personal Information) Act, 2003
laws.citation: Ch. 324A; s.2 physical or mental health is sensitive; s.17 Commissioner may restrict transfers, s.17(8) consent exempts

laws.name: Data Protection Act, 2025 (not yet in force)
laws.citation: Gazette 11 Dec 2025; s.35 written consent; s.36 health data only by or under a health care professional; ss.54-55 transfers

laws.name: Penal Code
laws.citation: Ch. 84, s.294 attempted suicide a misdemeanour

guidance_rules: If someone mentions a past or planned suicide attempt, respond supportively and never raise legality or suggest it will be reported; attempting suicide is still a misdemeanour in the Bahamas (Penal Code Ch. 84 s.294).
BS.regulator: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (https://dataprotection.gov.bs, site not verified)
BS.notes: 2003 Act still operative: health is sensitive but no extra safeguards were issued; consent exempts transfers (s.17(8)). The 2025 Act is on the official Not in Force list; commencement by Ministerial notice, possibly staged. Once in force, s.36 lets only a health care professional, or someone under a statutory secrecy duty, process health data, which would make Healthcare unavailable here; re-check monthly. Suicide offence per suicide-decrim.network, not re-verified against the Code.

DM.name: Dominica
DM.notes: No comprehensive data protection law found (UWI data protection resource, Feb 2025; no bill located since). Privacy rests on the Constitution and sectoral rules; no regulator. The OECS harmonised data protection effort (2022) has not produced a Dominica Act that we could find. No official Dominica legislation source was reached; re-check for a bill.

DO.name: Dominican Republic

laws.name: Ley No. 172-13 sobre Protección de Datos de Carácter Personal
laws.citation: 13 Dec 2013; Art. 6 health data sensitive; Art. 76 express written consent; Art. 80 international transfer with the person's free authorisation

DO.regulator: No data protection authority; Pro Consumidor hears consumer data complaints (no URL verified)
DO.notes: Ley 172-13 remains the framework; no replacement law found (El Nuevo Diario, 29 Jan 2026; older Senate draft of unknown status). Health data needs express written consent (Art. 76), so keep a recorded electronic opt-in; Art. 80 allows international transfer when the person freely authorises it. No authority for private processing; Pro Consumidor cannot fine. Text read via the Guzmán Ariza reproduction (official ONE PDF blocked).

GD.name: Grenada

laws.name: Data Protection Act, 2023 (not in force)
laws.citation: Act No. 1 of 2023; assented 9 May 2023, gazetted 10 May 2023, commencement by order

laws.name: Age of Civil Legal Responsibility Act, 2011
laws.citation: Act No. 14 of 2011; full civil capacity at 18

GD.regulator: None operating (Act provides for a commission not yet set up)
GD.notes: Data Protection Act No. 1 of 2023 was gazetted with no commencement date; no commencement order found, and a 2026 government document reportedly calls it not in force (OfflistMe review, 9 Oct 2026). Its text (sensitive categories, transfer rules) could not be read: the parliament site was unreachable. Age of majority is 18 under the Age of Civil Legal Responsibility Act 2011 (some lists wrongly say 21). Re-check commencement and the Act's health and transfer clauses.

HT.name: Haiti

laws.name: Arrêté fixant les règles relatives à la protection des données à caractère personnel
laws.citation: Le Moniteur No. 87, 15 May 2018; art. 4 bars releasing data that harms rights and freedoms

laws.name: Penal Code (reformed)
laws.citation: Data and cybercrime offences; entry into force reported for January 2027

HT.notes: No general data protection law or regulator. A 15 May 2018 arrêté sets basic rules; its scope is unclear. The reformed Penal Code with personal and sensitive data offences is reported (secondary sources, incl. a July 2026 UNDP notice) to enter into force in January 2027. Severe insecurity and a transitional government make enforcement unpredictable. Re-check once the Penal Code is in force.

JM.name: Jamaica

laws.name: Data Protection Act, 2020
laws.citation: Act 7 of 2020; s.2 health is sensitive; s.24(1)(a) consent in writing; s.31(4)(a) consent exception to the eighth standard; s.3(2) local representative; s.15 registration; s.20 DPO

laws.name: Data Protection (Data Controller Registration) Regulations, 2024
laws.citation: Registration with the Information Commissioner

JM.notes: Fully in force from 1 Dec 2023. Sensitive data needs consent in writing (s.24(1)(a)); keep a recorded electronic opt-in. Transfers: eighth standard (adequacy) with a consent exception (s.31(4)(a)). Back-end items: a controller offering services to people in Jamaica must appoint a local representative (s.3(2)), register before processing (s.15; OIC registration temporarily paused, Oct 2026) and appoint a DPO because it processes sensitive data (s.20(6)(b)).

KN.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis

laws.name: Data Protection Act, 2018 (not in force)
laws.citation: No. 5 of 2018; s.1(2) commencement by Ministerial order; s.2 health sensitive; s.20 explicit consent

KN.regulator: None operating (the Act designates the Information Commissioner)
KN.notes: Act No. 5 of 2018 (gazetted 7 June 2018) needs a Ministerial commencement order; none found (UWI, Feb 2025; later secondary checks), so no general law applies yet. On commencement health becomes sensitive with explicit consent (s.20), a non-resident controller using equipment in the Federation must nominate a local representative, and the Information Commissioner enforces. No transfer-abroad section seen. Re-check the Gazette.

LC.name: Saint Lucia

laws.name: Data Protection Act
laws.citation: Act 11 of 2011 as amended by Act 2 of 2015; partly in force 31 Jan 2023 (SI 4/2023); s.35(b)(i) explicit consent; s.37 health purposes; s.45 transfers (not in force)

laws.name: Criminal Code
laws.citation: s.94 attempted suicide an offence

guidance_rules: If someone mentions a past or planned suicide attempt, respond supportively and never raise legality or suggest it will be reported; attempting suicide is still an offence in Saint Lucia (Criminal Code s.94).
LC.regulator: Data Protection Commissioner (Part II not yet in force; no office or website found)
LC.notes: SI 4/2023 commenced only Part I, ss.32-43, Part VI and Sch. 2(a)-(g) from 31 Jan 2023: explicit consent for sensitive data (s.35(b)(i)) applies, but the Commissioner (Part II) and transfers (s.45) are not in force. When s.45 starts, every transfer abroad needs Commissioner authorisation (s.45(1)(b)); consent waives only the comparable-safeguards limb, so storage may then need to become transient. Suicide offence per suicide-decrim.network, not re-verified against the Code.

TT.name: Trinidad and Tobago

laws.name: Data Protection Act, 2011
laws.citation: Act 13 of 2011 (Chap. 22:04), partly proclaimed; s.2 health is sensitive; s.6(h) and (l) general privacy principles; Part IV private sector not in force

TT.regulator: Office of the Information Commissioner (established by s.7; no website or appointment confirmed)
TT.notes: Only Part I, ss.7-18, 22, 23, 25(1), 26, 28 and 42(a)-(b) are proclaimed (2012, 2021); private-sector duties (Part IV, incl. s.72 consent to transfers) and penalties are not, and no reform bill was found. In-force s.6 says sensitive data is 'protected from processing except where otherwise provided for by written law' (s.6(h)) and data sent abroad needs comparable safeguards (s.6(l)); no adequacy list exists. Persist kept because no in-force mechanism enforces these, but a literal reading is a risk.

VC.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

laws.name: Privacy Act, 2003 (not in force)
laws.citation: Public authorities only; never commenced

VC.notes: No general data protection law in force: the Privacy Act 2003 covers only public authorities and was never commenced (UWI, Feb 2025); no newer bill found. No regulator. No official SVG legislation source was reached; re-check for an OECS-model bill.

FM.name: Micronesia

laws.name: FSM Code Title 21, ss.349-350
laws.citation: Telecom providers must keep customer information confidential

laws.name: Personal Data Protection Act of 2025 (bill)
laws.citation: Congressional Bill 24-17; national government departments only

FM.notes: No general data protection law (DLA Piper, 2 Feb 2026). The Personal Data Protection Act of 2025 (CB 24-17) would cover national government departments only; a committee report followed hearings in late 2025 and passage is unconfirmed. State-level laws (Chuuk, Kosrae, Pohnpei, Yap) were not checked.

KI.name: Kiribati

laws.name: Data Protection Act 2025
laws.citation: s.2 commencement by notice; s.5(1)(b) applies to services offered to people in Kiribati; no sensitive category; s.24(a) informed consent for transfers

laws.name: Notice of Commencement, Data Protection Act
laws.citation: Gazette, scanned 24 Aug 2026

KI.regulator: Digital Transformation Office, Ministry of Information, Communications and Transport (https://mict.gov.ki/dto, not verified)
KI.notes: A Notice of Commencement was gazetted around 24 Aug 2026, but the scan could not be read, so the start date is unconfirmed. The Act has no sensitive-data category, hence 'personal'. Transfers without adequate protection need consent given after being told of the risks (s.24(a)), so the consent card should say US processing may lack equivalent protection; keep a record (s.25). The 2-year grace (s.6(2)) covers only local controllers. Age of majority unconfirmed; the Act treats under-18s as children (s.12).

MH.name: Marshall Islands

laws.name: Personal Data Protection Act 2025
laws.citation: P.L. 2025-43 (6 MIRC Ch. 4); s.403 core Government ministries and agencies only; s.418 effective 12 months after certification

MH.regulator: None for private services (EPSSO is the authority for government agencies)
MH.notes: The Personal Data Protection Act 2025 applies only to core Government ministries and agencies (s.403), so no general law reaches a private foreign service; health_data is 'personal'. Certification date, and so the government-sector effective date, not found. Text read from the Nitijela PDF.

NR.name: Nauru

laws.name: Cybercrime Act 2015
laws.citation: Computer offences only

laws.name: Communications and Broadcasting Act 2018
laws.citation: Subscriber information confidentiality

NR.notes: No general data protection law found; only the Cybercrime Act 2015 and subscriber confidentiality under the Communications and Broadcasting Act 2018, per a secondary source. No 2024-2026 bill found. No regulator. No official Nauru legislation source was reached.

PW.name: Palau
PW.notes: Sources conflict: one secondary site cites a c.2019 Privacy Act at 6 PNCA ss.205-206, but no official text was found and other sources (IAPP list, Dec 2021; 2025 guides) say Palau has no comprehensive law. Senate Bill 12-9 (Cybersecurity Act) passed the Senate in Oct 2025; enactment unconfirmed. Check the Palau National Code before relying on 'personal'.

TV.name: Tuvalu
TV.notes: No verified general data protection law; a 'Data Protection and Privacy Act 2020' appears only in unverified secondary sources and was not found on PacLII. A Cybercrime Bill was reported pending in May 2026. No regulator. Age of majority not confirmed; 18 used as the floor.

TL.name: Timor-Leste

laws.name: Constitution of the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste
laws.citation: Art. 38 protection of personal data; no implementing law

TL.notes: No general data protection law; Constitution art. 38 protects personal data but no implementing law exists (secondary sources, 2026). On 31 Jul 2026 the Government asked Parliament for legislative authorisation for a cybersecurity package that includes personal data and privacy rules; watch for decree-laws. Civil majority is reportedly 17, so 18 is used. No regulator.

PS.name: Palestine

laws.name: Cabinet Decision No. 3 of 2019 on citizens' personal data
laws.citation: Bars commercial use of citizens' personal data by service companies without prior permission

laws.name: Draft Decree-Law on Personal Data Protection (not enacted)
laws.citation: Third reading 15 June 2022; still before the Cabinet in Oct 2023

PS.notes: No data protection law: the draft decree-law (third reading June 2022) was still with the Cabinet in Oct 2023 and no enactment was found since. Cabinet Decision 3/2019 needs prior permission for commercial use of citizens' data (West Bank and Gaza). Majority age 18 rests on a scholarly reading of the Majalla. The Gaza war and divided governance make the position unstable; this covers PA-administered law only.

LY.name: Libya

laws.name: Law No. 6 of 2022 on Electronic Transactions
laws.citation: Arts. 73-84: explicit consent (art. 73), transfers with due regard to protection level (art. 78), penalties (arts. 81-84)

laws.name: Law No. 17 of 1992 on Minors
laws.citation: Art. 9 majority at 18 Gregorian years

laws.name: Law No. 5 of 2022 on Combating Cybercrime
laws.citation: Computer and content offences

LY.regulator: None (no data protection authority; NISSA policies bind state bodies only)
LY.notes: No dedicated data protection law or regulator. Law 6/2022 arts. 73-84 require explicit consent and due regard to the destination's protection level for transfers (art. 78), but may only cover e-certification services; health is not a special category (DLA Piper, Jan 2024; statute text not read). Rival governments and conflict make enforcement unpredictable. US sanctions on Libya are list-based, not comprehensive.
